content.intro: Learn handling form errors through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Handling Form Errors matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines handling form errors as part of forms and user input. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Field errors; Non-field errors; Error presentation; Accessibility of error messages; Troubleshooting failed submissions. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Field errors
items.text: Treat Field errors as a reproducible diagnostic: capture the exact input and observed result, isolate one hypothesis, and add a regression test once the cause is fixed. Avoid exposing internal stack traces or secrets to public users.

items.title: Accessibility of error messages
items.text: Accessible pages need semantic structure, associated labels, understandable errors, keyboard operation, visible focus and text alternatives. Verify these behaviors rather than relying on appearance alone.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
